decision_rationale: The objective asks for new synthetic cells for rare classes to support classification. The data are UMI-like counts (integers in [0, 419], 97.4% zeros, 96.7% of assessed genes overdispersed) with 8 classes and an imbalance ratio of 76.3. Two classes are far below the rest: Dendritic cells (37) and Megakaryocytes (15). A conditional count-likelihood VAE trained on all 2,638 cells can share structure across classes. That is a better basis for minority augmentation than interpolating among 15 or 37 cells. Megakaryocytes are close to the memorisation limit, so the plan caps augmentation, tracks memorisation and keeps class-weighting as a baseline that must be beaten.

task.raw_objective: Generate realistic synthetic cells for rare cell types to support downstream cell-type classification.

models.name: nb_vae
models.rationale: UMI counts are overdispersed integers (median var/mean 1.51; 96.7% of genes overdispersed). The NB likelihood fits the zeros well: excess zeros vs NB are -0.029, and ZINB is preferred for only 2.3% of genes. The observed library size (median 2,214) is used as an offset. A small network is used because n_train is about 1,850.

models.name: vae
models.rationale: Gaussian VAE on log-normalised expression, matched in size to the primary model. It tests whether the count likelihood actually helps.
